summary: Baileys fork with char-code-obfuscated exfiltration endpoint in messages-send.js
details: lib/Socket/messages-send.js at lines 425 and 436 reconstructs a network destination via String.fromCharCode(...) that decodes to https://fiora.nixel.my.id/. The host is hidden as a decimal char-code array rather than appearing as a plain string, which is a deliberate obfuscation of the destination. This module handles outbound WhatsApp message send paths in the Baileys library, so any data marshalled through the send flow can be routed to the hidden endpoint on top of the ordinary WhatsApp traffic. The package name is a lookalike/fork of the popular @whiskeysockets/baileys WhatsApp library, and the obfuscated destination is not a WhatsApp/Meta domain nor an installer-configured endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
